sections.content: How many people are "elementary process plant occupations (other)"?

85,690 people

were counted on the census as "elementary process plant occupations (other)" in England and Wales in March 2021.

People who do this type of work may assist the work of machine operatives and perform a variety of manual tasks in foundries, engineering and allied trades and in other process and plant operations not elsewhere classified.

People who had this job were generally similar in age to the working population

The occupation of "elementary process plant occupations (other)" had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 50 to 54 years. Of the whole working population 11.7% were aged 50 to 54 years. For people working as "elementary process plant occupations (other)", 13% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "elementary process plant occupations (other)" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "elementary process plant occupations (other)" included:

  • care workers and home carers
  • nursing auxiliaries and assistants
  • weighers, graders and sorters

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "elementary process plant occupations (other)" there were more men than women (78.3% compared with 21.7%).

This means "elementary process plant occupations (other)" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "elementary trades and related occupations".

Men made up 78.3% and women made up 21.7% of "elementary process plant occupations (other)"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "elementary process plant occupations (other)" included:

  • IT business analysts, architects and systems designers
  • parking and civil enforcement occupations
  • senior officers in fire, ambulance, prison and related services

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "elementary process plant occupations (other)" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Men and women with this occupation had a similar age profile, as shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "elementary process plant occupations (other)" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "elementary process plant occupations (other)", 8.4% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (86.7% compared with 13.3%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (95.4%) than self-employed (4.6%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the West Midlands. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included County Durham, this is in the region of the North East.
